1: //! # Symbol Table — Per-scope variable definition and usage tracking
2: //!
3: //! This module provides a [`SymbolTable`] that maps out every variable definition
4: //! and usage across all scopes in a MATLAB source file. It is the foundation for
5: //! rules that need scope-aware analysis such as unused variables, undefined
6: //! variables, and shadowed variables.
7: //!
8: //! ## How it works
9: //!
10: //! [`SymbolTable::build`] performs a single depth-first traversal of the
11: //! tree-sitter parse tree. It maintains a scope stack: every time it enters a
12: //! `function_definition` or `lambda`, a new [`Scope`] is pushed. When the
13: //! traversal leaves that node, the scope is popped.
14: //!
15: //! For each identifier encountered, the builder inspects the parent node to
16: //! decide whether the identifier is a **definition** ([`VarDef`]) or a
17: //! **usage** ([`VarUse`]). Definitions include input/output arguments,
18: //! assignment left-hand sides, for-loop iterators, `global`/`persistent`
19: //! declarations, nested function names, and lambda parameters. Everything
20: //! else is a usage.
21: //!
22: //! ## Example
23: //!
24: //! ```ignore
25: //! use tree_sitter::Parser;
26: //! use mlt_rules::analysis::symbols::SymbolTable;
27: //!
28: //! let source = "function y = foo(x)\n    y = x + 1;\nend\n";
29: //! let mut parser = Parser::new();
30: //! parser.set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into()).unwrap();
31: //! let tree = parser.parse(source, None).unwrap();
32: //!
33: //! let table = SymbolTable::build(&tree, source);
34: //! assert_eq!(table.scopes.len(), 1);
35: //! assert!(table.root_scope().is_defined("x"));
36: //! assert!(table.root_scope().is_defined("y"));
37: //! ```
38: 
39: use std::collections::HashSet;
40: use tree_sitter::Tree;
41: 
42: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
43: // Definition kinds
44: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45: 
46: /// The type of a variable definition.
47: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
48: pub enum DefKind {
49:     /// Function input argument.
50:     InputArg,
51:     /// Function output argument.
52:     OutputArg,
53:     /// Assignment left-hand side (`x = ...`).
54:     Assignment,
55:     /// For-loop iterator variable.
56:     ForIterator,
57:     /// Global declaration (`global x`).
58:     Global,
59:     /// Persistent declaration (`persistent x`).
60:     Persistent,
61:     /// Nested function name.
62:     NestedFunction,
63:     /// Anonymous function parameter.
64:     LambdaParam,
65: }
66: 
67: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68: // VarDef / VarUse
69: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70: 
71: /// A single variable definition occurrence.
72: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
73: pub struct VarDef {
74:     /// The variable name.
75:     pub name: String,
76:     /// How it was defined.
77:     pub kind: DefKind,
78:     /// Byte range in source.
79:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
80:     /// 1-indexed line number.
81:     pub line: usize,
82:     /// 1-indexed column number.
83:     pub column: usize,
84: }
85: 
86: /// A single variable usage (read) occurrence.
87: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
88: pub struct VarUse {
89:     /// The variable name.
90:     pub name: String,
91:     /// Byte range in source.
92:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
93:     /// 1-indexed line number.
94:     pub line: usize,
95:     /// 1-indexed column number.
96:     pub column: usize,
97: }
98: 
99: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100: // Scope
101: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102: 
103: /// The type of scope.
104: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
105: pub enum ScopeKind {
106:     /// File-level script scope (no enclosing function).
107:     Script,
108:     /// Main function (first `function_definition` in file).
109:     Function,
110:     /// Local function (subsequent `function_definition`s at file level).
111:     LocalFunction,
112:     /// Nested function (`function_definition` inside another function).
113:     NestedFunction,
114:     /// Method (`function_definition` inside a `methods` block in a class).
115:     Method,
116:     /// Anonymous function body.
117:     Lambda,
118: }
119: 
120: /// A scope representing a function, script, or lambda body.
121: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
122: pub struct Scope {
123:     /// The name of the function/method (empty string for scripts/lambdas).
124:     pub name: String,
125:     /// The kind of scope.
126:     pub kind: ScopeKind,
127:     /// Byte range of the entire scope node.
128:     pub byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
129:     /// 1-indexed line of scope start.
130:     pub line: usize,
131:     /// All variable definitions in this scope.
132:     pub defs: Vec<VarDef>,
133:     /// All variable usages (reads) in this scope.
134:     pub uses: Vec<VarUse>,
135:     /// Child scope indices (nested functions, lambdas).
136:     pub children: Vec<usize>,
137:     /// Parent scope index (`None` for top-level).
138:     pub parent: Option<usize>,
139: }
140: 
141: impl Scope {
142:     /// Get all definitions of a variable by name.
143:     pub fn defs_of(&self, name: &str) -> Vec<&VarDef> {
144:         self.defs.iter().filter(|d| d.name == name).collect()
145:     }
146: 
147:     /// Get all usages of a variable by name.
148:     pub fn uses_of(&self, name: &str) -> Vec<&VarUse> {
149:         self.uses.iter().filter(|u| u.name == name).collect()
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Get all unique defined variable names.
153:     pub fn defined_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
154:         let mut seen = HashSet::new();
155:         self.defs
156:             .iter()
157:             .filter_map(|d| {
158:                 if seen.insert(d.name.as_str()) {
159:                     Some(d.name.as_str())
160:                 } else {
161:                     None
162:                 }
163:             })
164:             .collect()
165:     }
166: 
167:     /// Get all unique used variable names.
168:     pub fn used_names(&self) -> Vec<&str> {
169:         let mut seen = HashSet::new();
170:         self.uses
171:             .iter()
172:             .filter_map(|u| {
173:                 if seen.insert(u.name.as_str()) {
174:                     Some(u.name.as_str())
175:                 } else {
176:                     None
177:                 }
178:             })
179:             .collect()
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Check if a variable is defined in this scope.
183:     pub fn is_defined(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
184:         self.defs.iter().any(|d| d.name == name)
185:     }
186: 
187:     /// Check if a variable is used in this scope.
188:     pub fn is_used(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
189:         self.uses.iter().any(|u| u.name == name)
190:     }
191: }
192: 
193: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
194: // SymbolTable
195: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
196: 
197: /// The complete symbol table for a file.
198: ///
199: /// Contains all scopes (functions, scripts, lambdas) in the file, each with
200: /// their own definitions and usages. Scopes are stored in a flat `Vec` and
201: /// reference each other by index via [`Scope::children`] and [`Scope::parent`].
202: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
203: pub struct SymbolTable {
204:     /// All scopes in the file, indexed by position in this vec.
205:     pub scopes: Vec<Scope>,
206: }
207: 
208: impl SymbolTable {
209:     /// Get the root/file-level scope (index 0).
210:     pub fn root_scope(&self) -> &Scope {
211:         &self.scopes[0]
212:     }
213: 
214:     /// Get all function-level scopes (excluding lambdas and the root script scope).
215:     pub fn function_scopes(&self) -> Vec<&Scope> {
216:         self.scopes
217:             .iter()
218:             .filter(|s| {
219:                 matches!(
220:                     s.kind,
221:                     ScopeKind::Function
222:                         | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
223:                         | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
224:                         | ScopeKind::Method
225:                 )
226:             })
227:             .collect()
228:     }
229: 
230:     /// Find the innermost scope containing a given byte offset.
231:     ///
232:     /// Searches all scopes and returns the smallest (innermost) one whose
233:     /// byte range contains `byte_offset`.
234:     pub fn scope_at(&self, byte_offset: usize) -> Option<&Scope> {
235:         self.scopes
236:             .iter()
237:             .filter(|s| s.byte_range.contains(&byte_offset))
238:             .min_by_key(|s| s.byte_range.end - s.byte_range.start)
239:     }
240: 
241:     /// Build a symbol table from a parsed tree and source text.
242:     ///
243:     /// Performs a single DFS traversal of the tree-sitter parse tree, tracking
244:     /// scopes and collecting variable definitions and usages.
245:     pub fn build(tree: &Tree, source: &str) -> Self {
246:         let mut builder = Builder {
247:             source,
248:             scopes: Vec::new(),
249:             scope_stack: Vec::new(),
250:             first_file_function_seen: false,
251:         };
252:         builder.run(tree);
253:         SymbolTable {
254:             scopes: builder.scopes,
255:         }
256:     }
257: }
258: 
259: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
260: // Builder (private)
261: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
262: 
263: /// Internal builder that drives the DFS traversal and populates scopes.
264: struct Builder<'a> {
265:     source: &'a str,
266:     scopes: Vec<Scope>,
267:     /// Stack of scope indices: the last element is the "current" scope.
268:     scope_stack: Vec<usize>,
269:     /// Whether we have seen the first file-level `function_definition`.
270:     first_file_function_seen: bool,
271: }
272: 
273: impl<'a> Builder<'a> {
274:     // -- scope helpers ------------------------------------------------------
275: 
276:     /// Push a new scope and return its index.
277:     fn push_scope(&mut self, scope: Scope) -> usize {
278:         let idx = self.scopes.len();
279:         // Wire up parent ↔ child.
280:         let parent = self.scope_stack.last().copied();
281:         let mut scope = scope;
282:         scope.parent = parent;
283:         if let Some(p) = parent {
284:             self.scopes[p].children.push(idx);
285:         }
286:         self.scopes.push(scope);
287:         self.scope_stack.push(idx);
288:         idx
289:     }
290: 
291:     /// Pop the current scope off the stack.
292:     fn pop_scope(&mut self) {
293:         self.scope_stack.pop();
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Index of the current scope, if any.
297:     fn current_scope(&self) -> Option<usize> {
298:         self.scope_stack.last().copied()
299:     }
300: 
301:     /// Add a definition to the current scope.
302:     fn add_def(&mut self, def: VarDef) {
303:         if let Some(idx) = self.current_scope() {
304:             self.scopes[idx].defs.push(def);
305:         }
306:     }
307: 
308:     /// Add a usage to the current scope.
309:     fn add_use(&mut self, var_use: VarUse) {
310:         if let Some(idx) = self.current_scope() {
311:             self.scopes[idx].uses.push(var_use);
312:         }
313:     }
314: 
315:     /// Extract the text of a node from source.
316:     fn node_text(&self, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> &'a str {
317:         &self.source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
318:     }
319: 
320:     // -- main entry ---------------------------------------------------------
321: 
322:     /// Run the full build.
323:     fn run(&mut self, tree: &'a Tree) {
324:         let root = tree.root_node();
325: 
326:         // Determine if this is a script or function file.
327:         // A function file starts with a `function_definition` as the first
328:         // meaningful child of `source_file`. Otherwise it's a script.
329:         let is_function_file = Self::first_meaningful_child_is_function(&root);
330: 
331:         if !is_function_file {
332:             // Script file: the entire file is one Script scope.
333:             let pos = root.start_position();
334:             self.push_scope(Scope {
335:                 name: String::new(),
336:                 kind: ScopeKind::Script,
337:                 byte_range: root.start_byte()..root.end_byte(),
338:                 line: pos.row + 1,
339:                 defs: Vec::new(),
340:                 uses: Vec::new(),
341:                 children: Vec::new(),
342:                 parent: None,
343:             });
344:         }
345: 
346:         // Walk children of source_file.
347:         self.visit_children(root);
348: 
349:         // If this was a function file and we never pushed a scope, that
350:         // shouldn't happen, but guard against it.
351:         if self.scopes.is_empty() {
352:             let pos = root.start_position();
353:             self.push_scope(Scope {
354:                 name: String::new(),
355:                 kind: ScopeKind::Script,
356:                 byte_range: root.start_byte()..root.end_byte(),
357:                 line: pos.row + 1,
358:                 defs: Vec::new(),
359:                 uses: Vec::new(),
360:                 children: Vec::new(),
361:                 parent: None,
362:             });
363:         }
364:     }
365: 
366:     /// Check if the first non-comment child of `source_file` is a function.
367:     fn first_meaningful_child_is_function(root: &tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
368:         let count = root.child_count();
369:         for i in 0..count {
370:             if let Some(child) = root.child(i) {
371:                 match child.kind() {
372:                     "comment" | "line_continuation" => continue,
373:                     "function_definition" => return true,
374:                     _ => return false,
375:                 }
376:             }
377:         }
378:         false
379:     }
380: 
381:     // -- recursive visitor --------------------------------------------------
382: 
383:     /// Visit all children of a node, dispatching each to the appropriate handler.
384:     fn visit_children(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
385:         let count = node.child_count();
386:         for i in 0..count {
387:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
388:                 self.visit_node(child);
389:             }
390:         }
391:     }
392: 
393:     /// Dispatch a single node.
394:     fn visit_node(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
395:         match node.kind() {
396:             "function_definition" => self.visit_function_definition(node),
397:             "lambda" => self.visit_lambda(node),
398:             "assignment" => self.visit_assignment(node),
399:             "for_statement" => self.visit_for_statement(node),
400:             "global_operator" => self.visit_global_persistent(node, DefKind::Global),
401:             "persistent_operator" => self.visit_global_persistent(node, DefKind::Persistent),
402:             "identifier" => self.visit_identifier(node),
403:             // For all other nodes, just recurse into children.
404:             _ => self.visit_children(node),
405:         }
406:     }
407: 
408:     // -- function_definition ------------------------------------------------
409: 
410:     /// Visit a `function_definition` node.
411:     ///
412:     /// Creates a new scope, extracts input/output args, then recurses into
413:     /// the function body. Nested functions and methods are distinguished by
414:     /// the current scope stack depth and parent node context.
415:     fn visit_function_definition(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
416:         let pos = node.start_position();
417: 
418:         // Extract function name.
419:         let func_name = node
420:             .child_by_field_name("name")
421:             .map(|n| self.node_text(n).to_string())
422:             .unwrap_or_default();
423: 
424:         // Determine scope kind.
425:         let scope_kind = self.classify_function_scope(node);
426: 
427:         // If this is a nested function, register its name as a def in the
428:         // parent scope (so the parent can "call" it).
429:         if scope_kind == ScopeKind::NestedFunction {
430:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
431:                 let name_pos = name_node.start_position();
432:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
433:                     name: func_name.clone(),
434:                     kind: DefKind::NestedFunction,
435:                     byte_range: name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte(),
436:                     line: name_pos.row + 1,
437:                     column: name_pos.column + 1,
438:                 });
439:             }
440:         }
441: 
442:         // Push new scope.
443:         self.push_scope(Scope {
444:             name: func_name,
445:             kind: scope_kind,
446:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
447:             line: pos.row + 1,
448:             defs: Vec::new(),
449:             uses: Vec::new(),
450:             children: Vec::new(),
451:             parent: None, // set by push_scope
452:         });
453: 
454:         // Extract output arguments.
455:         self.extract_function_outputs(node);
456: 
457:         // Extract input arguments.
458:         self.extract_function_inputs(node);
459: 
460:         // Recurse into the function body (all children except the ones we
461:         // already handled).
462:         let count = node.child_count();
463:         for i in 0..count {
464:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
465:                 let kind = child.kind();
466:                 if kind == "function_arguments" || kind == "function_output" {
467:                     // Already handled above.
468:                     continue;
469:                 }
470:                 if kind == "identifier" {
471:                     // Skip the function name identifier (it's the `name` field).
472:                     if node
473:                         .child_by_field_name("name")
474:                         .map(|n| n.id() == child.id())
475:                         .unwrap_or(false)
476:                     {
477:                         continue;
478:                     }
479:                 }
480:                 self.visit_node(child);
481:             }
482:         }
483: 
484:         self.pop_scope();
485:     }
486: 
487:     /// Classify a `function_definition` based on its position in the tree.
488:     fn classify_function_scope(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> ScopeKind {
489:         // Check if we're inside a `methods` block.
490:         if Self::is_inside_methods_block(node) {
491:             return ScopeKind::Method;
492:         }
493: 
494:         // Check if we're inside another function scope.
495:         if self
496:             .current_scope()
497:             .map(|idx| {
498:                 matches!(
499:                     self.scopes[idx].kind,
500:                     ScopeKind::Function
501:                         | ScopeKind::LocalFunction
502:                         | ScopeKind::NestedFunction
503:                         | ScopeKind::Method
504:                 )
505:             })
506:             .unwrap_or(false)
507:         {
508:             return ScopeKind::NestedFunction;
509:         }
510: 
511:         // File-level function.
512:         if !self.first_file_function_seen {
513:             self.first_file_function_seen = true;
514:             ScopeKind::Function
515:         } else {
516:             ScopeKind::LocalFunction
517:         }
518:     }
519: 
520:     /// Check if a node is inside a `methods` block (by walking parents).
521:     fn is_inside_methods_block(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
522:         let mut current = node.parent();
523:         while let Some(p) = current {
524:             if p.kind() == "methods" {
525:                 return true;
526:             }
527:             // Stop at class_definition level — don't walk further up.
528:             if p.kind() == "class_definition" || p.kind() == "source_file" {
529:                 break;
530:             }
531:             current = p.parent();
532:         }
533:         false
534:     }
535: 
536:     /// Extract output arguments from `function_output`.
537:     fn extract_function_outputs(&mut self, func_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
538:         let Some(output_node) = func_node.child_by_field_name("output") else {
539:             // Also try iterating children for "function_output".
540:             let count = func_node.child_count();
541:             for i in 0..count {
542:                 if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
543:                     if child.kind() == "function_output" {
544:                         self.extract_output_identifiers(child);
545:                         return;
546:                     }
547:                 }
548:             }
549:             return;
550:         };
551:         self.extract_output_identifiers(output_node);
552:     }
553: 
554:     /// Recursively extract identifiers from an output node.
555:     fn extract_output_identifiers(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
556:         match node.kind() {
557:             "identifier" => {
558:                 let pos = node.start_position();
559:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
560:                     name: self.node_text(node).to_string(),
561:                     kind: DefKind::OutputArg,
562:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
563:                     line: pos.row + 1,
564:                     column: pos.column + 1,
565:                 });
566:             }
567:             "multioutput_variable" | "function_output" => {
568:                 let count = node.child_count();
569:                 for i in 0..count {
570:                     if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
571:                         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
572:                             let pos = child.start_position();
573:                             self.add_def(VarDef {
574:                                 name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
575:                                 kind: DefKind::OutputArg,
576:                                 byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
577:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
578:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
579:                             });
580:                         } else if child.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
581:                             self.extract_output_identifiers(child);
582:                         }
583:                         // Skip `ignored_argument` (~).
584:                     }
585:                 }
586:             }
587:             _ => {}
588:         }
589:     }
590: 
591:     /// Extract input arguments from `function_arguments`.
592:     fn extract_function_inputs(&mut self, func_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
593:         let count = func_node.child_count();
594:         for i in 0..count {
595:             if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
596:                 if child.kind() == "function_arguments" {
597:                     self.extract_input_identifiers(child);
598:                     return;
599:                 }
600:             }
601:         }
602:     }
603: 
604:     /// Extract identifiers from a `function_arguments` node.
605:     fn extract_input_identifiers(&mut self, args_node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
606:         let count = args_node.child_count();
607:         for i in 0..count {
608:             if let Some(child) = args_node.child(i) {
609:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
610:                     let pos = child.start_position();
611:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
612:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
613:                         kind: DefKind::InputArg,
614:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
615:                         line: pos.row + 1,
616:                         column: pos.column + 1,
617:                     });
618:                 }
619:                 // Skip `ignored_argument` (~).
620:             }
621:         }
622:     }
623: 
624:     // -- lambda -------------------------------------------------------------
625: 
626:     /// Visit a `lambda` node (`@(x, y) expr`).
627:     ///
628:     /// Creates a Lambda scope, extracts parameters, then visits the body.
629:     fn visit_lambda(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
630:         let pos = node.start_position();
631: 
632:         self.push_scope(Scope {
633:             name: String::new(),
634:             kind: ScopeKind::Lambda,
635:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
636:             line: pos.row + 1,
637:             defs: Vec::new(),
638:             uses: Vec::new(),
639:             children: Vec::new(),
640:             parent: None, // set by push_scope
641:         });
642: 
643:         // Extract lambda parameters. In tree-sitter-matlab, the lambda's
644:         // arguments node contains the parameter identifiers.
645:         let count = node.child_count();
646:         for i in 0..count {
647:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
648:                 if child.kind() == "arguments" || child.kind() == "lambda_arguments" {
649:                     let arg_count = child.child_count();
650:                     for j in 0..arg_count {
651:                         if let Some(arg) = child.child(j) {
652:                             if arg.kind() == "identifier" {
653:                                 let arg_pos = arg.start_position();
654:                                 self.add_def(VarDef {
655:                                     name: self.node_text(arg).to_string(),
656:                                     kind: DefKind::LambdaParam,
657:                                     byte_range: arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte(),
658:                                     line: arg_pos.row + 1,
659:                                     column: arg_pos.column + 1,
660:                                 });
661:                             }
662:                         }
663:                     }
664:                 }
665:             }
666:         }
667: 
668:         // Visit body (all children that are not the arguments).
669:         for i in 0..count {
670:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
671:                 let kind = child.kind();
672:                 if kind == "arguments" || kind == "lambda_arguments" {
673:                     continue;
674:                 }
675:                 // Skip punctuation tokens like `@`, `(`, `)`.
676:                 if kind == "@" || kind == "(" || kind == ")" || kind == "," {
677:                     continue;
678:                 }
679:                 self.visit_node(child);
680:             }
681:         }
682: 
683:         self.pop_scope();
684:     }
685: 
686:     // -- assignment ---------------------------------------------------------
687: 
688:     /// Visit an `assignment` node.
689:     ///
690:     /// Extracts LHS identifiers as definitions, then visits the RHS as usages.
691:     fn visit_assignment(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
692:         // Process LHS: definitions.
693:         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
694:             self.extract_assignment_lhs(lhs);
695:         }
696: 
697:         // Process RHS: usages (just recurse normally).
698:         if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
699:             self.visit_node(rhs);
700:         }
701:     }
702: 
703:     /// Extract definitions from an assignment LHS.
704:     fn extract_assignment_lhs(&mut self, lhs: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
705:         match lhs.kind() {
706:             "identifier" => {
707:                 let pos = lhs.start_position();
708:                 self.add_def(VarDef {
709:                     name: self.node_text(lhs).to_string(),
710:                     kind: DefKind::Assignment,
711:                     byte_range: lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte(),
712:                     line: pos.row + 1,
713:                     column: pos.column + 1,
714:                 });
715:             }
716:             "multioutput_variable" => {
717:                 let count = lhs.child_count();
718:                 for i in 0..count {
719:                     if let Some(child) = lhs.child(i) {
720:                         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
721:                             let pos = child.start_position();
722:                             self.add_def(VarDef {
723:                                 name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
724:                                 kind: DefKind::Assignment,
725:                                 byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
726:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
727:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
728:                             });
729:                         }
730:                         // Skip `ignored_argument` (~) and punctuation.
731:                     }
732:                 }
733:             }
734:             "function_call" => {
735:                 // Indexed assignment: `A(i) = ...` or `obj.field = ...`.
736:                 // The name of the function_call is the variable being
737:                 // assigned into; we treat it as a usage (the variable must
738:                 // already exist). Arguments are usages too. Recurse normally.
739:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
740:             }
741:             "field_expression" => {
742:                 // `obj.field = ...` — `obj` is a usage.
743:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
744:             }
745:             "cell_index" => {
746:                 // `C{i} = ...` — treat like indexed assignment.
747:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
748:             }
749:             _ => {
750:                 // Unknown LHS shape — recurse for safety.
751:                 self.visit_node(lhs);
752:             }
753:         }
754:     }
755: 
756:     // -- for_statement ------------------------------------------------------
757: 
758:     /// Visit a `for_statement` node.
759:     ///
760:     /// Extracts the iterator variable as a definition, then visits the body.
761:     fn visit_for_statement(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
762:         // The for statement has an `iterator` child that contains the loop
763:         // variable and the range expression.
764:         let count = node.child_count();
765:         for i in 0..count {
766:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
767:                 if child.kind() == "iterator" {
768:                     self.visit_iterator(child);
769:                 } else {
770:                     self.visit_node(child);
771:                 }
772:             }
773:         }
774:     }
775: 
776:     /// Visit an `iterator` node inside a for-statement.
777:     ///
778:     /// The first identifier child is the loop variable (definition).
779:     /// Everything else (the range expression) is visited for usages.
780:     fn visit_iterator(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
781:         let mut found_var = false;
782:         let count = node.child_count();
783:         for i in 0..count {
784:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
785:                 if !found_var && child.kind() == "identifier" {
786:                     // This is the loop variable.
787:                     let pos = child.start_position();
788:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
789:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
790:                         kind: DefKind::ForIterator,
791:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
792:                         line: pos.row + 1,
793:                         column: pos.column + 1,
794:                     });
795:                     found_var = true;
796:                 } else if child.kind() == "=" {
797:                     // Skip the `=` token.
798:                     continue;
799:                 } else {
800:                     // Range expression — visit for usages.
801:                     self.visit_node(child);
802:                 }
803:             }
804:         }
805:     }
806: 
807:     // -- global / persistent ------------------------------------------------
808: 
809:     /// Visit a `global_operator` or `persistent_operator` node.
810:     ///
811:     /// Each child identifier is a declaration.
812:     fn visit_global_persistent(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>, kind: DefKind) {
813:         let count = node.child_count();
814:         for i in 0..count {
815:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
816:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
817:                     let pos = child.start_position();
818:                     self.add_def(VarDef {
819:                         name: self.node_text(child).to_string(),
820:                         kind,
821:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
822:                         line: pos.row + 1,
823:                         column: pos.column + 1,
824:                     });
825:                 }
826:             }
827:         }
828:     }
829: 
830:     // -- identifier (the tricky one) ----------------------------------------
831: 
832:     /// Visit a bare `identifier` node.
833:     ///
834:     /// Determines from parent context whether this identifier is a definition
835:     /// (already captured elsewhere), a function/field name (skip), or a
836:     /// genuine variable usage.
837:     fn visit_identifier(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node<'a>) {
838:         let Some(parent) = node.parent() else {
839:             // Orphan identifier — treat as usage to be safe.
840:             self.record_use(node);
841:             return;
842:         };
843: 
844:         match parent.kind() {
845:             // Already handled by visit_assignment.
846:             "assignment" => {
847:                 if parent
848:                     .child_by_field_name("left")
849:                     .map(|l| l.id() == node.id())
850:                     .unwrap_or(false)
851:                 {
852:                     // This is the simple LHS identifier — already captured.
853:                     return;
854:                 }
855:                 // Otherwise it's on the RHS — it's a usage.
856:                 self.record_use(node);
857:             }
858: 
859:             // Already handled by extract_assignment_lhs.
860:             "multioutput_variable" => {
861:                 // Check if the multioutput_variable is the LHS of an assignment.
862:                 if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
863:                     if grandparent.kind() == "assignment"
864:                         && grandparent
865:                             .child_by_field_name("left")
866:                             .map(|l| l.id() == parent.id())
867:                             .unwrap_or(false)
868:                     {
869:                         // Already captured as assignment def.
870:                         return;
871:                     }
872:                     // multioutput_variable in function_output context.
873:                     if grandparent.kind() == "function_output" {
874:                         return;
875:                     }
876:                 }
877:                 self.record_use(node);
878:             }
879: 
880:             // Function definition name — skip (not a variable usage).
881:             "function_definition" => {
882:                 if parent
883:                     .child_by_field_name("name")
884:                     .map(|n| n.id() == node.id())
885:                     .unwrap_or(false)
886:                 {
887:                     return;
888:                 }
889:                 // Could be a child that's not the name — e.g., part of
890:                 // the body that was somehow an identifier child. Visit as use.
891:                 self.record_use(node);
892:             }
893: 
894:             // function_arguments / function_output — already handled.
895:             "function_arguments" | "function_output" => {
896:                 // Already captured as InputArg / OutputArg.
897:             }
898: 
899:             // global/persistent — already handled.
900:             "global_operator" | "persistent_operator" => {
901:                 // Already captured as Global / Persistent.
902:             }
903: 
904:             // For-loop iterator — already handled.
905:             "iterator" => {
906:                 // Already captured as ForIterator. But the range expression
907:                 // identifiers also have parent `iterator`. We need to check if
908:                 // this is the first identifier (the loop var) or a later one.
909:                 // The first identifier child of `iterator` is the loop var.
910:                 let first_ident = Self::first_identifier_child(parent);
911:                 if first_ident.map(|n| n.id() == node.id()).unwrap_or(false) {
912:                     // This is the loop variable — already captured.
913:                     return;
914:                 }
915:                 // Otherwise it's part of the range expression.
916:                 self.record_use(node);
917:             }
918: 
919:             // Lambda arguments — already handled.
920:             "arguments" | "lambda_arguments" => {
921:                 // Only skip if the parent's parent is a lambda.
922:                 if let Some(grandparent) = parent.parent() {
923:                     if grandparent.kind() == "lambda" {
924:                         return;
925:                     }
926:                 }
927:                 self.record_use(node);
928:             }
929: 
930:             // Function call name: count as usage (could be array indexing).
931:             "function_call" => {
932:                 // The `name` field of function_call should be counted as a
933:                 // usage because it could be array indexing (`A(i)`), where
934:                 // `A` must be defined.
935:                 self.record_use(node);
936:             }
937: 
938:             // Field expression: only the `object` part is a usage, not the
939:             // `field` part.
940:             "field_expression" => {
941:                 if parent
942:                     .child_by_field_name("field")
943:                     .map(|f| f.id() == node.id())
944:                     .unwrap_or(false)
945:                 {
946:                     // This is the field name (e.g., `field` in `obj.field`).
947:                     // Not a standalone variable usage.
948:                     return;
949:                 }
950:                 // This is the object part — it's a usage.
951:                 self.record_use(node);
952:             }
953: 
954:             // Class definition name — skip.
955:             "class_definition" => {
956:                 if parent
957:                     .child_by_field_name("name")
958:                     .map(|n| n.id() == node.id())
959:                     .unwrap_or(false)
960:                 {
961:                     return;
962:                 }
963:                 self.record_use(node);
964:             }
965: 
966:             // Default: it's a variable usage.
967:             _ => {
968:                 self.record_use(node);
969:             }
970:         }
971:     }
972: 
973:     /// Find the first `identifier` child of a node.
974:     fn first_identifier_child(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> Option<tree_sitter::Node> {
975:         let count = node.child_count();
976:         for i in 0..count {
977:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
978:                 if child.kind() == "identifier" {
979:                     return Some(child);
980:                 }
981:             }
982:         }
983:         None
984:     }
985: 
986:     /// Record a variable usage at the given identifier node.
987:     fn record_use(&mut self, node: tree_sitter::Node) {
988:         let pos = node.start_position();
989:         self.add_use(VarUse {
990:             name: self.node_text(node).to_string(),
991:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
992:             line: pos.row + 1,
993:             column: pos.column + 1,
994:         });
995:     }
996: }

147: /// Provides the parsed tree (for rules that need their own traversal strategy),
148: /// the full source text, and the file path.
149: pub struct FileContext<'a> {
150:     pub tree: &'a Tree,
151:     pub source: &'a str,
152:     pub file_path: &'a Path,
153: }
154: 
155: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156: // Rule trait
157: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158: 
159: /// The core trait that all lint rules must implement.
160: ///
161: /// Rules declare which tree-sitter node types they are interested in via
162: /// [`target_node_types`]. During the single-pass traversal, the engine
163: /// dispatches matching nodes to [`check`]. After traversal, [`check_file`]
164: /// is called on rules that override it for file-level analysis.
165: ///
166: /// # Design Notes
167: ///
168: /// - **Node-level rules**: Override `check()`, return `target_node_types()`.
169: /// - **File-level rules**: Override `check_file()`, return empty `target_node_types()`.
170: /// - **Hybrid rules**: Override both (unusual, but supported).
171: ///
172: /// Rules must be `Send + Sync` to support future parallel file processing.
173: pub trait Rule: Send + Sync {
174:     /// Unique rule identifier matching MATLAB Code Analyzer check IDs
175:     /// (e.g., `"NOSEMI"`, `"AGROW"`, `"naming.class.casing"`).
176:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
177: 
178:     /// Human-readable one-line description of what this rule checks.
179:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str;
180: 
181:     /// Default severity for diagnostics produced by this rule.
182:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity;
183: 
184:     /// The category this rule belongs to (used for bulk config).
185:     fn category(&self) -> Category;
186: 
187:     /// Tree-sitter node type names this rule subscribes to.
188:     ///
189:     /// Return an empty slice for file-level-only rules (which use `check_file`).
190:     /// The engine uses this to build an index for O(1) dispatch during traversal.
191:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str];
192: 
193:     /// Whether this rule can be disabled by the user. Most rules return `true`.
194:     /// The 17 "Incomplete Analysis" checks cannot be disabled.
195:     fn can_be_disabled(&self) -> bool {
196:         true
197:     }
198: 
199:     /// Whether this rule implements file-level checking.
200:     ///
201:     /// Override to return `true` if the rule implements [`check_file`].
202:     /// This allows the engine to skip calling `check_file()` on rules
203:     /// that only do node-level checking.
204:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
205:         false
206:     }
207: 
208:     /// Check a single node encountered during the single-pass traversal.
209:     ///
210:     /// Only called for nodes whose `kind()` is in [`target_node_types`].
211:     /// Default implementation returns no diagnostics.
212:     fn check(&self, _ctx: &NodeContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
213:         Vec::new()
214:     }
215: 
216:     /// Check the file after the full traversal has completed.
217:     ///
218:     /// Called once per file for rules where [`has_file_check`] returns `true`.
219:     /// Use this for rules that require full-file context (e.g., unused variables,
220:     /// duplicate definitions). Default implementation returns no diagnostics.
221:     fn check_file(&self, _ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
222:         Vec::new()
223:     }
224: }

1: //! # Function/Class Metadata Extraction
2: //!
3: //! Extracts structural metadata from a parsed MATLAB file, including:
4: //!
5: //! - **File type** detection (script, function file, class file)
6: //! - **Function metadata**: name, inputs, outputs, argument validation blocks,
7: //!   setter/getter/constructor detection, method attributes
8: //! - **Class metadata**: name, superclasses, attributes, properties blocks,
9: //!   methods blocks, events blocks, enumeration blocks
10: //! - **Property metadata**: name, dimensions, type constraints, validators,
11: //!   default values
12: //!
13: //! ## Usage
14: //!
15: //! ```ignore
16: //! use mlt_rules::analysis::metadata::FileMeta;
17: //!
18: //! let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
19: //! match meta.file_type {
20: //!     FileType::ClassFile => {
21: //!         let class = meta.class.as_ref().unwrap();
22: //!         println!("Class: {}", class.name);
23: //!         for prop in meta.all_properties() {
24: //!             println!("  property: {}", prop.name);
25: //!         }
26: //!     }
27: //!     FileType::FunctionFile => {
28: //!         if let Some(main) = meta.main_function() {
29: //!             println!("Main function: {}", main.name);
30: //!         }
31: //!     }
32: //!     FileType::Script => println!("Script file"),
33: //! }
34: //! ```

36: use std::ops::Range;
37: use tree_sitter::{Node, Tree};
38: 
39: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
40: // Core types
41: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
42: 
43: /// The type of MATLAB file.
44: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
45: pub enum FileType {
46:     /// Script file (no `function_definition` at top level, or function after statements).
47:     Script,
48:     /// Function file (starts with `function_definition`).
49:     FunctionFile,
50:     /// Class definition file (contains `class_definition`).
51:     ClassFile,
52: }
53: 
54: /// Metadata about a function definition.
55: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
56: pub struct FunctionMeta {
57:     /// Function name.
58:     pub name: String,
59:     /// Input argument names.
60:     pub inputs: Vec<String>,
61:     /// Output argument names (includes `~` as placeholder).
62:     pub outputs: Vec<String>,
63:     /// Whether this is a constructor (name matches class name).
64:     pub is_constructor: bool,
65:     /// Whether this is a property setter (name starts with `set.`).
66:     pub is_setter: bool,
67:     /// Whether this is a property getter (name starts with `get.`).
68:     pub is_getter: bool,
69:     /// Whether this function has an `arguments` validation block.
70:     pub has_arguments_block: bool,
71:     /// The argument validation entries (if any).
72:     pub argument_validations: Vec<ArgValidation>,
73:     /// Byte range of the function node.
74:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
75:     /// 1-indexed start line.
76:     pub line: usize,
77:     /// 1-indexed end line.
78:     pub end_line: usize,
79:     /// Whether defined inside a methods block (is a method).
80:     pub is_method: bool,
81:     /// Whether this is an abstract method (`function_signature`, no body).
82:     pub is_abstract: bool,
83:     /// Attributes from the enclosing methods block (if any).
84:     pub method_attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
85: }
86: 
87: /// An argument validation entry from an `arguments` block.
88: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
89: pub struct ArgValidation {
90:     /// Argument name.
91:     pub name: String,
92:     /// Size constraint (e.g., `"(1,3)"`), if specified.
93:     pub dimensions: Option<String>,
94:     /// Class/type constraint (e.g., `"double"`), if specified.
95:     pub type_constraint: Option<String>,
96:     /// Validation functions (e.g., `["mustBePositive"]`).
97:     pub validators: Vec<String>,
98:     /// Default value expression text, if specified.
99:     pub default_value: Option<String>,
100: }
101: 
102: /// An attribute on a class, properties block, methods block, or events block.
103: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
104: pub struct AttributeMeta {
105:     /// Attribute name (e.g., `"Access"`, `"Sealed"`, `"Abstract"`).
106:     pub name: String,
107:     /// Attribute value as source text (e.g., `"private"`, `"true"`), or `None` if bare/negated.
108:     pub value: Option<String>,
109:     /// Whether the attribute is negated (e.g., `~Hidden`).
110:     pub negated: bool,
111: }
112: 
113: /// Metadata about a class property.
114: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
115: pub struct PropertyMeta {
116:     /// Property name.
117:     pub name: String,
118:     /// Size constraint, if specified.
119:     pub dimensions: Option<String>,
120:     /// Type constraint, if specified.
121:     pub type_constraint: Option<String>,
122:     /// Validation functions.
123:     pub validators: Vec<String>,
124:     /// Default value expression text.
125:     pub default_value: Option<String>,
126:     /// Whether this property has a default value.
127:     pub has_default: bool,
128:     /// Byte range.
129:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
130:     /// 1-indexed line.
131:     pub line: usize,
132: }
133: 
134: /// Metadata about a `properties ... end` block.
135: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
136: pub struct PropertiesBlockMeta {
137:     /// Attributes on this properties block.
138:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
139:     /// Properties defined in this block.
140:     pub properties: Vec<PropertyMeta>,
141: }
142: 
143: /// Metadata about a `methods ... end` block.
144: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
145: pub struct MethodsBlockMeta {
146:     /// Attributes on this methods block.
147:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
148:     /// Functions (methods) defined in this block.
149:     pub methods: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
150: }
151: 
152: /// Metadata about an `events ... end` block.
153: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
154: pub struct EventsBlockMeta {
155:     /// Attributes on this events block.
156:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
157:     /// Event names.
158:     pub events: Vec<String>,
159: }
160: 
161: /// Metadata about an `enumeration ... end` block.
162: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
163: pub struct EnumerationBlockMeta {
164:     /// Enumeration member names.
165:     pub members: Vec<String>,
166: }
167: 
168: /// Metadata about a class definition.
169: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
170: pub struct ClassMeta {
171:     /// Class name.
172:     pub name: String,
173:     /// Superclass names.
174:     pub superclasses: Vec<String>,
175:     /// Class-level attributes.
176:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
177:     /// Properties blocks.
178:     pub properties_blocks: Vec<PropertiesBlockMeta>,
179:     /// Methods blocks.
180:     pub methods_blocks: Vec<MethodsBlockMeta>,
181:     /// Events blocks.
182:     pub events_blocks: Vec<EventsBlockMeta>,
183:     /// Enumeration blocks.
184:     pub enumeration_blocks: Vec<EnumerationBlockMeta>,
185:     /// Byte range of the `class_definition` node.
186:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
187:     /// 1-indexed start line.
188:     pub line: usize,
189: }
190: 
191: /// Complete file metadata extracted from a single parse tree.
192: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
193: pub struct FileMeta {
194:     /// The type of this file (script, function, or class).
195:     pub file_type: FileType,
196:     /// The class definition, if this is a class file.
197:     pub class: Option<ClassMeta>,
198:     /// All function definitions (including methods if class file).
199:     /// For function files: first is the main function, rest are local functions.
200:     pub functions: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
201:     /// Local functions defined after the class definition (in class files)
202:     /// or after the main function (in function files).
203:     pub local_functions: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
204: }
205: 
206: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
207: // Helpers
208: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
209: 
210: /// Extract the source text covered by a node.
211: fn node_text<'a>(node: Node, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
212:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
213: }
214: 
215: /// Extract attributes from an `attributes` node.
216: ///
217: /// Each `attribute` child represents a single attribute entry.
218: /// Attributes can be:
219: /// - Bare: `Sealed` (value is `None`, treated as `true`)
220: /// - Valued: `Access = private`
221: /// - Negated: `~Hidden` (negated flag set)
222: fn extract_attributes(attrs_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<AttributeMeta> {
223:     let mut attrs = Vec::new();
224:     let mut cursor = attrs_node.walk();
225: 
226:     for child in attrs_node.children(&mut cursor) {
227:         if child.kind() != "attribute" {
228:             continue;
229:         }
230: 
231:         let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
232:         let negated = text.starts_with('~');
233: 
234:         // Find the attribute name — first identifier child.
235:         let name = find_first_child_of_kind(child, "identifier")
236:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())
237:             .unwrap_or_default();
238: 
239:         if name.is_empty() {
240:             continue;
241:         }
242: 
243:         // Look for `= value` portion.  The value is everything after the `=`.
244:         // In the grammar an attribute with a value has the identifier, then `=`, then
245:         // one or more value children (which may be identifiers, strings, etc.).
246:         let value = extract_attribute_value(child, source);
247: 
248:         attrs.push(AttributeMeta {
249:             name,
250:             value,
251:             negated,
252:         });
253:     }
254: 
255:     attrs
256: }
257: 
258: /// Extract the value portion of an `attribute` node (everything after `=`).
259: ///
260: /// Returns `None` if no `=` is present (bare attribute).
261: fn extract_attribute_value(attr_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
262:     let mut found_eq = false;
263:     let mut cursor = attr_node.walk();
264: 
265:     for child in attr_node.children(&mut cursor) {
266:         let kind = child.kind();
267:         let text = node_text(child, source);
268: 
269:         if text == "=" {
270:             found_eq = true;
271:             continue;
272:         }
273: 
274:         if found_eq && kind != "=" {
275:             // Capture the first meaningful token after `=` as the value.
276:             return Some(text.trim().to_string());
277:         }
278:     }
279: 
280:     None
281: }
282: 
283: /// Find the first child of a node with the given kind.
284: fn find_first_child_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
285:     let child_count = node.child_count();
286:     for i in 0..child_count {
287:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
288:             if child.kind() == kind {
289:                 return Some(child);
290:             }
291:         }
292:     }
293:     None
294: }
295: 
296: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
297: // Function extraction
298: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
299: 
300: /// Build the full function name, including `set.` or `get.` prefix if present.
301: ///
302: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, `function set.Value(...)` produces:
303: /// - a child node with kind `set.`
304: /// - the `name` field pointing to the `identifier` node `Value`
305: ///
306: /// This function checks for that prefix and prepends it to the base name.
307: fn build_function_name(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
308:     let name_node = func_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
309:     let base_name = node_text(name_node, source);
310: 
311:     // Check for `set.` or `get.` prefix child.
312:     let child_count = func_node.child_count();
313:     for i in 0..child_count {
314:         if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
315:             let kind = child.kind();
316:             if kind == "set." || kind == "get." {
317:                 return Some(format!("{}{}", kind, base_name));
318:             }
319:         }
320:     }
321: 
322:     Some(base_name.to_string())
323: }
324: 
325: /// Extract metadata from a `function_definition` node.
326: fn extract_function_meta(
327:     node: Node,
328:     source: &str,
329:     class_name: Option<&str>,
330:     is_method: bool,
331:     method_attributes: &[AttributeMeta],
332:     is_abstract: bool,
333: ) -> Option<FunctionMeta> {
334:     let name = build_function_name(node, source)?;
335: 
336:     let inputs = extract_function_inputs(node, source);
337:     let outputs = extract_function_outputs(node, source);
338: 
339:     let is_constructor = class_name.is_some_and(|cn| cn == name);
340:     let is_setter = name.starts_with("set.");
341:     let is_getter = name.starts_with("get.");
342: 
343:     let (has_arguments_block, argument_validations) = extract_arguments_blocks(node, source);
344: 
345:     Some(FunctionMeta {
346:         name,
347:         inputs,
348:         outputs,
349:         is_constructor,
350:         is_setter,
351:         is_getter,
352:         has_arguments_block,
353:         argument_validations,
354:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
355:         line: node.start_position().row + 1,
356:         end_line: node.end_position().row + 1,
357:         is_method,
358:         is_abstract,
359:         method_attributes: method_attributes.to_vec(),
360:     })
361: }
362: 
363: /// Extract a `function_signature` (abstract method stub with no body).
364: fn extract_function_signature(
365:     node: Node,
366:     source: &str,
367:     class_name: Option<&str>,
368:     method_attributes: &[AttributeMeta],
369: ) -> Option<FunctionMeta> {
370:     let name = build_function_name(node, source)?;
371: 
372:     let inputs = extract_function_inputs(node, source);
373:     let outputs = extract_function_outputs(node, source);
374: 
375:     let is_constructor = class_name.is_some_and(|cn| cn == name);
376:     let is_setter = name.starts_with("set.");
377:     let is_getter = name.starts_with("get.");
378: 
379:     Some(FunctionMeta {
380:         name,
381:         inputs,
382:         outputs,
383:         is_constructor,
384:         is_setter,
385:         is_getter,
386:         has_arguments_block: false,
387:         argument_validations: Vec::new(),
388:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
389:         line: node.start_position().row + 1,
390:         end_line: node.end_position().row + 1,
391:         is_method: true,
392:         is_abstract: true,
393:         method_attributes: method_attributes.to_vec(),
394:     })
395: }
396: 
397: /// Extract input argument names from a function definition.
398: fn extract_function_inputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
399:     let mut names = Vec::new();
400:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
401: 
402:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
403:         if child.kind() == "function_arguments" {
404:             let mut inner = child.walk();
405:             for param in child.children(&mut inner) {
406:                 match param.kind() {
407:                     "identifier" => {
408:                         names.push(node_text(param, source).to_string());
409:                     }
410:                     "ignored_argument" => {
411:                         names.push("~".to_string());
412:                     }
413:                     _ => {}
414:                 }
415:             }
416:             break;
417:         }
418:     }
419: 
420:     names
421: }
422: 
423: /// Extract output argument names from a function definition.
424: fn extract_function_outputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
425:     let mut names = Vec::new();
426:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
427: 
428:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
429:         if child.kind() == "function_output" {
430:             let mut inner = child.walk();
431:             for out_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
432:                 match out_child.kind() {
433:                     "identifier" => {
434:                         names.push(node_text(out_child, source).to_string());
435:                     }
436:                     "ignored_argument" => {
437:                         names.push("~".to_string());
438:                     }
439:                     "multioutput_variable" => {
440:                         let mut mv_cursor = out_child.walk();
441:                         for mv_child in out_child.children(&mut mv_cursor) {
442:                             match mv_child.kind() {
443:                                 "identifier" => {
444:                                     names.push(node_text(mv_child, source).to_string());
445:                                 }
446:                                 "ignored_argument" => {
447:                                     names.push("~".to_string());
448:                                 }
449:                                 _ => {}
450:                             }
451:                         }
452:                     }
453:                     _ => {}
454:                 }
455:             }
456:             break;
457:         }
458:     }
459: 
460:     names
461: }
462: 
463: /// Extract `arguments` validation blocks from within a function definition.
464: ///
465: /// Returns `(has_arguments_block, validations)`.
466: fn extract_arguments_blocks(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> (bool, Vec<ArgValidation>) {
467:     let mut validations = Vec::new();
468:     let mut found = false;
469: 
470:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
471:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
472:         if child.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
473:             found = true;
474:             // Each `property` child inside the arguments block describes one argument.
475:             let mut inner = child.walk();
476:             for arg_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
477:                 if arg_child.kind() == "property" {
478:                     if let Some(validation) = extract_arg_validation(arg_child, source) {
479:                         validations.push(validation);
480:                     }
481:                 }
482:             }
483:         }
484:     }
485: 
486:     (found, validations)
487: }
488: 
489: /// Extract a single argument validation entry from a `property` node inside
490: /// an `arguments` block.
491: fn extract_arg_validation(prop_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ArgValidation> {
492:     let name = prop_node
493:         .child_by_field_name("name")
494:         .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "identifier"))
495:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())?;
496: 
497:     let dimensions = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "dimensions")
498:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
499: 
500:     // Type constraint: bare identifier after dimensions (not the name).
501:     let type_constraint = extract_type_constraint(prop_node, source, &name);
502: 
503:     let validators = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "validation_functions")
504:         .map(|vf| {
505:             let mut v = Vec::new();
506:             let mut vc = vf.walk();
507:             for vchild in vf.children(&mut vc) {
508:                 if vchild.kind() == "identifier" {
509:                     v.push(node_text(vchild, source).to_string());
510:                 }
511:             }
512:             v
513:         })
514:         .unwrap_or_default();
515: 
516:     let default_value = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "default_value")
517:         .map(|dv| {
518:             // The actual expression is the child(ren) after `=`.
519:             // Use the full text, trimming the leading `=` if present.
520:             let text = node_text(dv, source).trim().to_string();
521:             let text = text.strip_prefix('=').unwrap_or(&text).trim().to_string();
522:             text
523:         });
524: 
525:     Some(ArgValidation {
526:         name,
527:         dimensions,
528:         type_constraint,
529:         validators,
530:         default_value,
531:     })
532: }
533: 
534: /// Extract the type constraint from a property node.
535: ///
536: /// In MATLAB, the property syntax is: `name (dims) type {validators} = default`.
537: /// The type is a bare identifier (or `property_name` for dotted names)
538: /// that appears after dimensions but before validation_functions/default_value.
539: fn extract_type_constraint(prop_node: Node, source: &str, prop_name: &str) -> Option<String> {
540:     let mut cursor = prop_node.walk();
541:     let mut past_name = false;
542:     let mut past_dims = false;
543: 
544:     for child in prop_node.children(&mut cursor) {
545:         let kind = child.kind();
546: 
547:         // Skip the name identifier.
548:         if !past_name {
549:             if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
550:                 let text = node_text(child, source);
551:                 if text == prop_name {
552:                     past_name = true;
553:                     continue;
554:                 }
555:             }
556:             continue;
557:         }
558: 
559:         // Skip dimensions.
560:         if kind == "dimensions" {
561:             past_dims = true;
562:             continue;
563:         }
564: 
565:         // If we haven't seen dimensions yet and we encounter an identifier,
566:         // it could still be the type (dimensions are optional).
567:         if !past_dims && kind == "dimensions" {
568:             continue;
569:         }
570: 
571:         // The type constraint is the first identifier/property_name after
572:         // the property name (and optional dimensions).
573:         if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
574:             return Some(node_text(child, source).to_string());
575:         }
576: 
577:         // If we hit validation_functions or default_value, no type was specified.
578:         if kind == "validation_functions" || kind == "default_value" || kind == "=" {
579:             return None;
580:         }
581:     }
582: 
583:     None
584: }
585: 
586: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
587: // Property extraction
588: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
589: 
590: /// Extract property metadata from a `property` node inside a `properties` block.
591: fn extract_property_meta(prop_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<PropertyMeta> {
592:     let name = prop_node
593:         .child_by_field_name("name")
594:         .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "identifier"))
595:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())?;
596: 
597:     let dimensions = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "dimensions")
598:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
599: 
600:     let type_constraint = extract_type_constraint(prop_node, source, &name);
601: 
602:     let validators = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "validation_functions")
603:         .map(|vf| {
604:             let mut v = Vec::new();
605:             let mut vc = vf.walk();
606:             for vchild in vf.children(&mut vc) {
607:                 if vchild.kind() == "identifier" {
608:                     v.push(node_text(vchild, source).to_string());
609:                 }
610:             }
611:             v
612:         })
613:         .unwrap_or_default();
614: 
615:     let default_value_node = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "default_value");
616:     let has_default = default_value_node.is_some();
617:     let default_value = default_value_node.map(|dv| {
618:         let text = node_text(dv, source).trim().to_string();
619:         let text = text.strip_prefix('=').unwrap_or(&text).trim().to_string();
620:         text
621:     });
622: 
623:     Some(PropertyMeta {
624:         name,
625:         dimensions,
626:         type_constraint,
627:         validators,
628:         default_value,
629:         has_default,
630:         byte_range: prop_node.start_byte()..prop_node.end_byte(),
631:         line: prop_node.start_position().row + 1,
632:     })
633: }
634: 
635: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
636: // Class extraction
637: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
638: 
639: /// Extract class metadata from a `class_definition` node.
640: fn extract_class_meta(class_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ClassMeta> {
641:     let name_node = class_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
642:     let class_name = node_text(name_node, source).to_string();
643: 
644:     // Superclasses.
645:     let superclasses = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "superclasses")
646:         .map(|sc| {
647:             let mut names = Vec::new();
648:             let mut cursor = sc.walk();
649:             for child in sc.children(&mut cursor) {
650:                 match child.kind() {
651:                     "identifier" | "property_name" => {
652:                         names.push(node_text(child, source).to_string());
653:                     }
654:                     _ => {}
655:                 }
656:             }
657:             names
658:         })
659:         .unwrap_or_default();
660: 
661:     // Class-level attributes.
662:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "attributes")
663:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
664:         .unwrap_or_default();
665: 
666:     // Collect section blocks.
667:     let mut properties_blocks = Vec::new();
668:     let mut methods_blocks = Vec::new();
669:     let mut events_blocks = Vec::new();
670:     let mut enumeration_blocks = Vec::new();
671: 
672:     let mut cursor = class_node.walk();
673:     for child in class_node.children(&mut cursor) {
674:         match child.kind() {
675:             "properties" => {
676:                 properties_blocks.push(extract_properties_block(child, source));
677:             }
678:             "methods" => {
679:                 methods_blocks.push(extract_methods_block(child, source, &class_name));
680:             }
681:             "events" => {
682:                 events_blocks.push(extract_events_block(child, source));
683:             }
684:             "enumeration" => {
685:                 enumeration_blocks.push(extract_enumeration_block(child, source));
686:             }
687:             _ => {}
688:         }
689:     }
690: 
691:     Some(ClassMeta {
692:         name: class_name,
693:         superclasses,
694:         attributes,
695:         properties_blocks,
696:         methods_blocks,
697:         events_blocks,
698:         enumeration_blocks,
699:         byte_range: class_node.start_byte()..class_node.end_byte(),
700:         line: class_node.start_position().row + 1,
701:     })
702: }
703: 
704: /// Extract a `properties ... end` block.
705: fn extract_properties_block(props_node: Node, source: &str) -> PropertiesBlockMeta {
706:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(props_node, "attributes")
707:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
708:         .unwrap_or_default();
709: 
710:     let mut properties = Vec::new();
711:     let mut cursor = props_node.walk();
712:     for child in props_node.children(&mut cursor) {
713:         if child.kind() == "property" {
714:             if let Some(pm) = extract_property_meta(child, source) {
715:                 properties.push(pm);
716:             }
717:         }
718:     }
719: 
720:     PropertiesBlockMeta {
721:         attributes,
722:         properties,
723:     }
724: }
725: 
726: /// Extract a `methods ... end` block.
727: fn extract_methods_block(methods_node: Node, source: &str, class_name: &str) -> MethodsBlockMeta {
728:     let block_attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(methods_node, "attributes")
729:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
730:         .unwrap_or_default();
731: 
732:     let mut methods = Vec::new();
733:     let mut cursor = methods_node.walk();
734:     for child in methods_node.children(&mut cursor) {
735:         match child.kind() {
736:             "function_definition" => {
737:                 if let Some(fm) = extract_function_meta(
738:                     child,
739:                     source,
740:                     Some(class_name),
741:                     true,
742:                     &block_attributes,
743:                     false,
744:                 ) {
745:                     methods.push(fm);
746:                 }
747:             }
748:             "function_signature" => {
749:                 if let Some(fm) =
750:                     extract_function_signature(child, source, Some(class_name), &block_attributes)
751:                 {
752:                     methods.push(fm);
753:                 }
754:             }
755:             _ => {}
756:         }
757:     }
758: 
759:     MethodsBlockMeta {
760:         attributes: block_attributes,
761:         methods,
762:     }
763: }
764: 
765: /// Extract an `events ... end` block.
766: fn extract_events_block(events_node: Node, source: &str) -> EventsBlockMeta {
767:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(events_node, "attributes")
768:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
769:         .unwrap_or_default();
770: 
771:     let mut events = Vec::new();
772:     let mut cursor = events_node.walk();
773:     for child in events_node.children(&mut cursor) {
774:         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
775:             events.push(node_text(child, source).to_string());
776:         }
777:     }
778: 
779:     EventsBlockMeta { attributes, events }
780: }
781: 
782: /// Extract an `enumeration ... end` block.
783: fn extract_enumeration_block(enum_node: Node, source: &str) -> EnumerationBlockMeta {
784:     let mut members = Vec::new();
785:     let mut cursor = enum_node.walk();
786:     for child in enum_node.children(&mut cursor) {
787:         if child.kind() == "enum" {
788:             // The enum member name is the first identifier child or "name" field.
789:             let name = child
790:                 .child_by_field_name("name")
791:                 .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(child, "identifier"))
792:                 .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
793:             if let Some(n) = name {
794:                 members.push(n);
795:             }
796:         }
797:     }
798: 
799:     EnumerationBlockMeta { members }
800: }
